findings.text: Installer for Xen HVM configuration of a virtual machine that validates caller supplied description and replaces stored configuration on success.
Delivery service for Xen event channel signals described by routing entry that validates port and priority and submits channel request.
System privilege translation service that resolves guest virtual address to guest physical address through the vCPU page walker.
Emulated cache writeback service that performs required writeback work and then advances past the emulated instruction.
Dedicated Xen mutex is held while sampling prior configuration and installing replacement description to serialize concurrent updates.
Current CPU is pinned while updating dirty mask and issuing broadcast on platforms with dedicated exit support, then released and mask cleared.
Directional accessor bundle groups a guest memory callback and a memory mapped IO callback together with a mutating direction indicator.
Deferred fragment observation carries target physical location and length with either inline value storage for small writes or reference to caller storage.
Global Xen enablement tracking increments when selector moves from disabled to enabled and schedules deferred decrement on the reverse move.
Clock update broadcast to all CPUs is requested exactly when unstable clock option differs between prior and replacement configuration.

Emulated access lifecycle first attempts direct guest handling for unknown regions, then in kernel resolution, then defers remainder to userspace. Reads stall for value while writes continue with deferred exit after emulation.
Read completion flag short circuits repeat emulation to tracing and clearing with no further memory work.
Pending PIO count distinguishes completion phase with buffered copy out from issue phase with fresh request.
Fetch service for emulator instruction bytes with fetch origin tagging and single page containment.
Standard data access services for emulator reads and writes with privilege aware attribute construction.
Memory mapped IO capable access services for reads, writes and compare exchange with paging, fragment and atomic handling.
Processor state services for control registers and debug registers queried and updated by the emulator.
Descriptor, segment, model specific register, counter, halt, intercept, CPUID and capability services queried by the emulator.
Side effect services for port IO, page invalidate and cache writeback invoked by the emulator.
Only subsets of three permitted option bits are accepted. Presence of any additional bit causes invalid argument failure.
Hypercall interception option excludes separate blob location and extent. Joint provision causes invalid argument failure.
Synthetic selector is either disabled value or confined to reserved virtualization range. Outside values cause invalid argument failure.
Port must be nonzero and below implementation maximum and priority must select two level mode. Violation causes invalid argument failure.
Positive delivery indication and masked channel indication are both normalized to overall success.
Channel descriptor is prepared with caller port and vCPU identity and placeholder index and caller priority before submission.
Translation uses neutral access attributes to express system origin.
Fetch translation tags user privilege when current privilege equals user level and always tags fetch origin. Invalid translation propagates as fault.
System origin tags implicit access. Non system origin tags user privilege when current privilege equals user level. Writes additionally tag mutating intent.
Local APIC page base is always classified as emulated memory mapped IO regardless of matcher outcome.
Fast virtual match synthesizes physical address from cached frame combined with page offset when paging is inactive or permission screening passes.
General resolution tags user privilege and mutating intent appropriately and distinguishes invalid translation from memory mapped IO classification.
Guest read reports inverted status of underlying read. Guest write reports failure distinctly and records write tracking on success.
Prior fault physical value is reused only when marked available and usable and page offset coincides with current address.
Access spanning page boundary is divided at boundary with address truncation when not in sixty four bit mode.
Small mutating remainder retains copied value locally while larger remainder references caller storage.
Atomic fast path is limited to power of two widths up to eight bytes and to accesses contained within single detection granularity.
Target frame is marked dirty before match outcome is determined, so mismatch still records write.
Control register support is limited to five documented indices with low half replacement for two of them and direct or delegated handling for others. Unknown index logs and fails.
Segment query always provides selector and reports usability. Unusable yields cleared description and false indication.
Segment install rebuilds base and limit with granularity expansion and copies attributes, marking absent as unusable with cleared padding.
Debug register queries and updates delegate to host helpers for effective and direct values.

Privilege, descriptor table, segment base, model specific register, counter, intercept, CPUID permission and lookup, and guest capability queries delegate to host services, while halt records a request flag.
Port output, page invalidate and writeback emulator hooks delegate directly to host services without extra policy.
Writeback is skipped when not required. When required, broadcast with CPU mask is used when exit support exists and local operation is used when it does not.
Port input completion copies buffered bytes to destination and emits trace and clears pending count.
Port input hook completes pending userspace round when count is nonzero and ignores caller count mismatch, otherwise it starts fresh operation.
Error logging helper prefixes messages with fixed tag and current task identifier.
Width specific user compare exchange wrapper selects operation width and fault handling token derived from width.
Host user memory access failure is historically treated as memory mapped IO even when backing slot exists.
Large and read accesses must avoid caller stack storage. Violation is treated as unhandleable.
Fragment accumulation assumes a bound on fragment count with overflow flagged by assertion.
Fault physical reuse retains only initial address and is therefore unsafe for repeated string operations.
Split detection granularity crossing, unmapped host address, invalid translation and APIC targeting all degrade atomic attempt to plain write emulation.
Mismatch still dirties and conservatively logs target as written per ABI that all writes are logged.
Fetch request crossing page end is truncated to page remainder with overflow flagged.
Userspace repeat count modification after exit is ignored as repeat count changes are unsupported.
Permitted HVM options comprise interception and send and unstable clock indicators.
Synthetic selector bounds delimit reserved virtualization range with zero meaning disabled.
Two level priority identifier is the sole accepted event channel priority.
Default APIC physical base identifies emulated page for both general classification and atomic exclusion.
Access attribute indicators distinguish user privilege and mutating intent and fetch origin and implicit system origin.
Emulator outcome indicators distinguish continue and input needed and fault propagation and unhandleable and compare mismatch.
Fragment limit bounds deferred pieces and eight byte threshold selects inline value storage.
Page size and mask define containment and offset extraction and frame conversion throughout translation.
Supported control register numbers are zero and two and three and four and eight.
